_read_me: MO2 Tool Runner - THEME TEMPLATE. Every value below is the current default theme (black and gold).
A theme is one copy of this file with new values: keep every key, change only the "value" fields (and the numbers / glyphs).
Put the theme file (and its icon, if it has one) in the "Themes" folder inside MO2 Tool Runner's data folder; Settings > THE WINDOW'S LOOK picks it.
A key left out keeps the default; a value that does not read is named in Settings and the default kept.
Colours are #RRGGBB, or #AARRGGBB where AA is opacity (00 see-through ... FF solid). Fonts are Windows font names, a fallback after a comma.
Each "where" line says where on screen the value shows, so a theme can be judged without running the program.
Rules a theme must keep: Text and Muted readable on Bg, Panel and Panel2 (contrast 4.5 : 1 or more); Good, Warn and Bad told apart
without colour alone being the only cue (each also has its own glyph); Accent readable on Panel2 (outlined buttons); the primary button's
text readable on its gradient. The window layout (where things sit) is not part of a theme - only how they look.

description.value: The default: near-black panels, gold accents.
description.where: one line under the name in Settings

windowsMode.where: Dark or Light - the base Windows draws text boxes, lists, scroll bars and drop-downs with

Bg.where: the window's background behind every panel

Panel.where: cards (the step list, the 'now running' card, the log), the header bar, the status bar, the Settings / History drawer, dialogs

Panel2.where: insides: text boxes, the log box, the history list, outlined buttons, unticked check boxes

Line.where: thin borders around cards, under the header, above the status bar

Accent.where: section headings (STEPS, LOG, THIS SETUP ...), ticked check boxes, the progress bar's end, the drawer's edge

AccentLight.where: the big step title, outlined-button text, hover and keyboard-focus outlines

AccentDim.where: outlined-button borders, unticked check-box borders, the drawer's left edge

Text.where: all normal text: step names, the activity line, settings, the log

Muted.where: secondary text: step notes, usual times, hints, the footer's shortcuts, field explanations

Good.where: a finished step's tick, 'finished' verdicts, 'Ready', MO2 / Skyrim status dot when fine

Warn.where: stopped runs, notes from the pre-check, 'a newer version is out'

Bad.where: failed steps, refusals, errors, the Stop now button's text, the interrupted-run banner's edge

OnAccent.where: text and the tick drawn ON accent: the START / primary button text, the tick inside a ticked check box

HoverFill.where: an outlined button's background while the mouse is over it

BannerBad.where: the 'last run did not finish - Put my profile back' banner across the top

GuidedFill.where: the box that asks the player to do an in-game step ('Your turn in the game')

Shade.where: the dimming over the window while the Settings or History drawer is open

PrimaryAndProgress.where: the START / Save / Put my profile back buttons and the progress bar of a running step

windowsAccent.where: the colour Windows' own controls use (focused text boxes, drop-down highlights, selected list rows) - lightest to darkest

Ui.value: Segoe UI Variable Text, Segoe UI

Heading.where: the program's name, section headings, the step title, primary buttons

sizes._note: Heading1 is also the program's name in the header; Clock is the run's elapsed time at the top right of the running step

glyphs.where: the mark at the end of each step row

statusDots.where: the two dots in the status bar take their colours from the list above: Mod Organizer open = Warn, Skyrim running = Bad, either one closed = Muted

icon.where: an .ico or .png file beside the theme file (empty = the program's own): the 30 x 30 logo left of the program's name and the window's taskbar / title-bar icon (the notification-area icon stays the program's own)

_not_in_a_theme: the layout: header, step list on the left, the running step and the log on the right, the status bar, the drawers
the words on screen (labels, messages, the readme)
sounds: the run-finished sound is Windows' own notification sound
